label: “; however,” / “. However,” — however starts clause 2 ｜ however 置於第二句句首

qs.passage: Monarch butterflies travel up to 4,800 kilometers each autumn to reach their wintering grounds in central Mexico. For decades, researchers assumed the insects relied mainly on the sun to find their way. The sun is an unreliable guide on cloudy ______ monarchs still manage to stay on course when skies are overcast. Later studies found that the butterflies can also sense Earth's magnetic field. This backup system may explain how the migration survives unpredictable autumn weather.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses joined by "however" need a semicolon (or period) BEFORE it and a comma AFTER it. A comma alone = comma splice; no comma after "however" is also wrong.
qs.mk: [1|The sun is an unreliable guide on cloudy days]⟨;⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2|monarchs still manage to stay on course] [d|when skies are overcast].

qs.passage: For much of the twentieth century, scientists believed that adult human brains could not grow new neurons. Brain cells, they thought, were formed only before birth and in early childhood. The idea seemed to match what doctors observed in patients with brain ______ studies in the 1990s found evidence that new neurons can form in the adult hippocampus, a region linked to memory. The extent of this process in humans is still debated. Even so, the discovery transformed how scientists think about learning and recovery.
qs.exp: A period before "However" and a comma after it correctly separates the two sentences. ", however," between two clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The idea seemed to match what doctors observed in patients with brain injuries]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [2|studies in the 1990s found evidence that new neurons can form in the adult hippocampus, a region linked to memory].

qs.passage: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean world. Silk was among the most famous goods carried along these routes. Merchants also traded spices, glass, horses, and ______ ideas and technologies may have been the network's most lasting cargo. Buddhism, for example, spread from India into China along these routes. Papermaking techniques later traveled west, reaching the Islamic world by the eighth century.
qs.exp: Between two independent clauses, "however" needs a semicolon before and a comma after. A comma before it = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Merchants also traded spices, glass, horses, and paper]⟨;⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2|ideas and technologies may have been the network's most lasting cargo].

qs.passage: Glass appears to be a solid, and in everyday life it behaves like one. A popular myth claims that glass is actually a slow-moving liquid. As evidence, people point to old church windows that are thicker at the bottom than at the ______ the uneven thickness was caused by the way old glass was made, not by centuries of slow flow. Glassmakers often installed the panes with the thicker edge at the bottom for stability. Calculations show that glass at room temperature would take far longer than the age of the universe to flow noticeably.
qs.exp: Period before "However," comma after it. ", however," between two independent clauses = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|As evidence, people point to old church windows that are thicker at the bottom than at the top]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [2|the uneven thickness was caused by the way old glass was made, not by centuries of slow flow].

The wood has survived because the oxygen-poor mud prevents decay. Over the centuries, though, the city has slowly sunk while sea levels have risen. In 2020, Venice began operating movable barriers to block high tides from the ______ the barriers are costly to raise, and critics worry that frequent closures could harm the lagoon's ecosystem.

qs.mk: [1|In 2020, Venice began operating movable barriers to block high tides from the Adriatic]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [2|the barriers are costly to raise, and critics worry that frequent closures could harm the lagoon's ecosystem].

qs.mk: [p|As a teenager in Paris,] [1|he learned a system of raised dots designed for soldiers to read messages at night]⟨;⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2|the system was too complicated for most readers].

qs.passage: William Shakespeare wrote about 37 plays between roughly 1590 and 1613. Many of them were performed at the Globe Theatre in London. qs.mk: [1|The plays were popular during his lifetime]⟨.⟩ {However}⟨,⟩ [2|only about half of them were printed before his death in 1616].

qs.mk: [1|The bark works because it contains a compound called salicin]⟨;⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2|the compound can cause stomach irritation when taken in large amounts].

qs.passage: The world's oceans absorb about a quarter of the carbon dioxide released by human activities. This process slows global ______ it also makes seawater more acidic. label: “, however;” — however ends clause 1 ｜ however 置於第一句句尾

qs.passage: Community gardens have spread rapidly through American cities over the past two decades. Supporters often describe them as a simple way to increase access to fresh produce. For many city planners, that finding alone justifies the modest public investment the gardens require.
qs.exp: Here "however" ends the first clause (contrasting it with the previous sentence), so it takes ", however;" and the semicolon separates the two independent clauses. ", however," creates a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The gardens' nutritional impact is difficult to measure]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|their social effects are easier to document].

qs.passage: Smartphones contain small amounts of gold, silver, and copper. Recovering these metals from discarded phones could reduce the need for new mining. qs.mk: [1|Recycling rates for electronics remain low]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|most old phones end up forgotten in drawers or thrown away with regular trash].

qs.mk: [1|Domestication probably did not begin with people choosing to keep cats as pets]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|cats likely moved into early farming villages on their own to hunt the mice that fed on stored grain].

qs.mk: [1|They are not entirely free of environmental costs]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨;⟩ [2|their spinning blades kill hundreds of thousands of birds in the United States each year].

label: “, however,” — however interrupts one clause ｜ however 插入句中

qs.passage: Johann Sebastian Bach was admired in his lifetime mainly as an organist rather than as a composer. After his death in 1750, much of his music was rarely performed. The young composer ______ helped change that in 1829 when he conducted a revival of the St. Matthew Passion in Berlin. The performance drew large crowds and sparked new interest in Bach's work across Europe. Today, Bach is regarded as one of the greatest composers in Western history.
qs.exp: "However" interrupts a single clause (subject … verb), so it needs a PAIR of commas. A semicolon would cut the subject off from its verb.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The young composer Felix Mendelssohn]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|helped change that in 1829] [d|when he conducted a revival of the St. Matthew Passion in Berlin].

qs.mk: [1:Subject|Opportunity]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|continued exploring for nearly fifteen years].

qs.exp: The semicolon already separates the clauses; inside the second clause, "however" interrupts subject and verb, so it needs a pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1|Scientists monitor the area constantly for signs of change]⟨;⟩ [2:Subject|a major eruption]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [2:Verb|is considered extremely unlikely in the near future].

qs.mk: [1:Subject|The Hawaiian Islands]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|formed far from any plate boundary].

qs.passage: Vaccines train the immune system to recognize a specific virus or bacterium. In theory, a vaccine could protect everyone who receives it. qs.mk: [1:Subject|The crowds]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|brought warmth, moisture, and carbon dioxide that damaged the paintings].

qs.passage: Gold is one of the least reactive metals. It does not rust or tarnish, which is why ancient gold jewelry still shines today. Pure gold ______ too soft for most everyday uses. Jewelers therefore mix it with other metals such as copper and silver. The purity of gold is measured in karats, with 24-karat gold being pure.
qs.exp: "However" interrupts the verb and its complement within one clause: pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|Pure gold is]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Complement|too soft for most everyday uses].

qs.passage: Saffron is made from the dried stigmas of the crocus flower. Each flower produces only three stigmas, which must be picked by hand. About 150,000 flowers are needed to produce a single kilogram of saffron. As a result, saffron is one of the most expensive spices in the world. Its high ______ has not stopped cooks around the world from using it in dishes such as Spanish paella and Persian rice.
qs.exp: "However" interrupts subject ("Its high price") and verb ("has not stopped"): pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Its high price]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|has not stopped cooks around the world from using it in dishes such as Spanish paella and Persian rice].

qs.passage: Latin has had no native speakers for more than a thousand years. The ______ remains surprisingly alive in science, law, and medicine. Biologists use Latin names to classify every known species. Lawyers still use Latin phrases such as habeas corpus. Many English words, including "audio" and "video," come directly from Latin verbs.
qs.exp: "However" interrupts subject ("The language") and verb ("remains"): pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The language]⟨,⟩ {however}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|remains surprisingly alive in science, law, and medicine].

label: though: adverb (= however) vs. conjunction (= although) ｜ though 副詞 vs. 連接詞

qs.passage: Octopuses are famous for solving puzzles in laboratory tanks, and some can even unscrew jar lids to reach food. In several ways, their intelligence resembles that of mammals such as dogs. The organization of that intelligence is very ______ about two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms rather than in its brain. Each arm can taste, touch, and react to its surroundings with surprising independence. Researchers are still investigating how the brain and the arms coordinate their activity.
qs.exp: "Though" here is an adverb meaning "however" that ends the first clause, so it works like ", however;". "; though + clause" makes "though" a conjunction and leaves a fragment after the semicolon.
qs.mk: [1|The organization of that intelligence is very different]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|about two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms rather than in its brain].

qs.passage: Emily Dickinson wrote nearly 1,800 poems during her lifetime. Fewer than a dozen of them were published while she was alive, and most of those appeared without her name. Though she rarely left her family's home in Amherst, ______ she exchanged letters with dozens of friends, editors, and relatives. These letters reveal a sharp, witty writer deeply engaged with the ideas of her time. After her death in 1886, her sister Lavinia discovered the hidden poems and worked to have them published.
qs.exp: "Though" is a subordinating conjunction here (= although). Dependent clause + COMMA + independent clause. A semicolon, period, or colon would leave the "Though" clause as a fragment.
qs.mk: «Though»[d|she rarely left her family's home in Amherst, Massachusetts]⟨,⟩ [1|she exchanged letters with dozens of friends, editors, and relatives].

qs.passage: The Maya city of Tikal once supported tens of thousands of residents. Its stone temples rise more than 60 meters above the surrounding rainforest. The city's population declined sharply in the ninth ______ archaeologists are still debating the causes. Some point to prolonged droughts, while others emphasize warfare and political instability. Most researchers now believe that several factors worked together.
qs.exp: "Though" = however, ending the first clause: ", though;". "; though + clause" turns "though" into a conjunction and leaves a fragment; ", though," is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The city's population declined sharply in the ninth century]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|archaeologists are still debating the causes].

qs.passage: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began tilting during its construction in the twelfth century. Builders had placed it on soft, unstable soil. Over the centuries, the lean grew so severe that engineers closed the tower to visitors in 1990. A decade of careful work removed soil from beneath the higher ______ though the tower still leans about four degrees today. Engineers estimate that it will remain stable for at least two hundred years.
qs.exp: "Though" here is a conjunction (= although) introducing a dependent clause after the main clause; a comma is correct. A semicolon, period, or colon leaves "though the tower…" as a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|A decade of careful work removed soil from beneath the higher side]⟨,⟩ «though»[d|the tower still leans about four degrees today].

qs.passage: Most people picture the Sahara as an endless sea of sand dunes. Dunes cover only about a quarter of the ______ of the rest consists of rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains. The desert's highest peak, Emi Koussi in Chad, rises more than 3,400 meters. Thousands of years ago, the Sahara was much greener than it is today. Rock paintings show giraffes, cattle, and even swimmers in places that are now completely dry.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) can end a sentence after a comma: ", though." Then a new sentence begins. ", though, much" is a comma splice; "; though much…" leaves a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|Dunes cover only about a quarter of the desert]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|Much of the rest consists of rocky plateaus, gravel plains, and mountains].

qs.passage: Electric cars produce no tailpipe emissions while they are being driven. Building their large ______ requires mining lithium, cobalt, and nickel, which can damage local environments. Researchers are developing batteries that use more common materials, such as sodium. Recycling old batteries could also reduce the need for new mining. Over its full lifetime, a typical electric car still produces fewer emissions than a comparable gasoline car.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) interrupts the subject and verb of one clause, so it needs a pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Building their large batteries]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|requires mining lithium, cobalt, and nickel]⟨,⟩ [d:nonessential|which can damage local environments].

qs.passage: The violin was developed in northern Italy in the early 1500s. Instruments made by Antonio Stradivari around 1700 are among the most valuable in the world. Many musicians claim that a Stradivarius has an unmatched sound. Listeners in blind tests have struggled to tell the ______ in several studies, professional violinists actually preferred new instruments. Some researchers argue that a famous instrument's reputation shapes how listeners hear it.
qs.exp: "Though" = however, ending the first clause → ", though;". ", though," is a comma splice; no punctuation is a run-on.
qs.mk: [1|Listeners in blind tests have struggled to tell the difference]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|in several studies, professional violinists actually preferred new instruments].

qs.passage: Sharks have existed for more than 400 million years, longer than trees have. They have survived several mass extinctions. Their ______ is far from certain. Each year, tens of millions of sharks are caught, many for their fins. Because most shark species grow slowly and produce few young, their populations recover very slowly from overfishing.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) interrupts the subject "future" and the verb "is," so it needs commas on both sides.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Their future]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|is far from certain].

qs.passage: Goldfish are often said to have memories lasting only three seconds. The claim is repeated in jokes, cartoons, and even advertisements. It has no scientific ______ laboratory experiments, goldfish have learned to push levers for food and remembered the task for months. Some fish have even learned to respond to particular sounds at feeding time. Scientists now consider goldfish surprisingly capable learners.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) ends the sentence: ", though." A new sentence begins with "In." ", though, in…" is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|It has no scientific basis]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|In laboratory experiments, goldfish have learned to push levers for food and remembered the task for months].

qs.passage: Antarctica is the coldest, windiest, and highest continent on average. Its ice sheet averages nearly two kilometers thick. Surprisingly, Antarctica is also the largest desert on ______ though it holds about 70 percent of the planet's fresh water. Most of the interior receives less than 50 millimeters of precipitation a year. The continent is classified as a desert because so little new snow falls there.
qs.exp: "Though" here is a conjunction (= although) introducing a dependent clause; join it with a comma. A period, semicolon, or colon creates a fragment.
qs.mk: {Surprisingly}, [1|Antarctica is also the largest desert on Earth]⟨,⟩ «though»[d|it holds about 70 percent of the planet's fresh water].

qs.passage: Desalination plants turn seawater into drinking water. The technology is especially important in dry countries such as Saudi Arabia and Israel. The process requires a great deal of energy; its leftover ______ may be the bigger environmental concern. Brine is about twice as salty as seawater and can form oxygen-poor layers on the sea floor. Engineers are testing ways to dilute the brine or extract useful minerals from it.
qs.exp: The semicolon separates the clauses; inside the second clause, "though" (= however) interrupts subject and verb, so it needs a pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1|The process requires a great deal of energy]⟨;⟩ [2:Subject|its leftover brine]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [2:Verb|may be the bigger environmental concern].

qs.passage: The Dutch tulip craze of the 1630s is often described as the first financial bubble. According to popular accounts, people sold houses to buy single tulip bulbs. Prices for rare bulbs did rise ______ historians have found little evidence that the crash ruined many people. Most buyers were wealthy merchants who could absorb their losses. Some historians argue that the story was exaggerated by moralists who disapproved of speculation.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) ends the first clause → ", though;". "; though + clause" leaves a fragment; ", though," = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Prices for rare bulbs did rise dramatically]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|historians have found little evidence that the crash ruined many people].

qs.passage: Planting trees is often promoted as a simple way to fight climate change. Trees absorb carbon dioxide as they grow and store carbon in their wood. Planting the wrong trees in the wrong ______ can do more harm than good. In grasslands, for example, dense tree plantations can use up scarce water and crowd out native species. Many scientists argue that protecting existing forests is more effective than planting new ones.
qs.exp: "Though" interrupts the subject ("Planting…places") and verb ("can do"): pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Planting the wrong trees in the wrong places]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|can do more harm than good].

qs.passage: Bananas contain potassium, a mineral the body needs. A tiny fraction of natural potassium is radioactive. As a result, bananas are very slightly radioactive. There is no need to give up ______ person would have to eat millions of bananas at once to receive a dangerous dose. The body also regulates its potassium levels, so eating more bananas does not cause radiation to build up.
qs.exp: ", though." ends the sentence (though = however). ", though, a…" is a comma splice; "; though a…" leaves a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|There is no need to give up bananas]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|A person would have to eat millions of bananas at once to receive a dangerous dose].

qs.passage: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh, a young astronomer working in Arizona. For decades, it was taught as the ninth planet in our solar system. The International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in ______ even though many people objected to the change. The decision followed the discovery of other icy objects of similar size beyond Neptune. To be considered a planet, an object must clear other material from its orbit, which Pluto has not done.
qs.exp: "Even though" introduces a dependent clause after the main clause; a comma is fine, but a semicolon, period, or colon leaves a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|The International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006]⟨,⟩ «even though»[d|many people objected to the change].

qs.passage: A cheetah can accelerate from 0 to about 95 kilometers per hour in roughly three seconds. Its flexible spine and long legs allow it to cover up to seven meters in a single stride. Though the cheetah is the fastest land ______ it can maintain its top speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds. After a chase, it must rest before eating, and larger predators sometimes steal its meal. For this reason, cheetahs often hunt during the day, when lions and hyenas are less active.
qs.exp: "Though" (conjunction) + dependent clause + COMMA + main clause. Adding "however" is redundant and creates an error.
qs.mk: «Though»[d|the cheetah is the fastest land animal]⟨,⟩ [1|it can maintain its top speed for only about 20 to 30 seconds].

qs.passage: Titan is the largest of Saturn's many moons. It is even bigger than the planet Mercury. Though smaller than ______ Titan has an atmosphere that is denser than Earth's. Its surface contains lakes and seas, but they are filled with liquid methane and ethane rather than water. NASA plans to send a drone-like spacecraft called Dragonfly to explore Titan in the 2030s.
qs.exp: "Though smaller than Mars" is a shortened dependent clause; follow it with a comma before the main clause.
qs.mk: «Though»[d:shortened clause|smaller than Mars]⟨,⟩ [1|Titan has an atmosphere that is denser than Earth's].

qs.passage: Most adults need seven to nine hours of sleep each night. ______ need even more, about eight to ten hours. During adolescence, the body's internal clock shifts later, making it hard for teens to fall asleep early. Many high schools start classes before 8:00 a.m., forcing students to wake up before they are fully rested. Some school districts have moved start times later and reported improved attendance and grades.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) interrupts subject and verb: pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Teenagers]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|need even more][p|, about eight to ten hours].

qs.passage: Robots have taken over many repetitive tasks in car factories and warehouses. They can weld, paint, and lift heavy parts with great precision. Folding laundry remains surprisingly difficult for ______ soft fabrics bend and change shape in unpredictable ways. A robot must recognize each item and plan a new sequence of movements for it. Several companies have built laundry-folding machines, but most have been too slow or expensive to succeed.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) ends the first clause → ", though;".
qs.mk: [1|Folding laundry remains surprisingly difficult for them]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨;⟩ [2|soft fabrics bend and change shape in unpredictable ways].

qs.passage: Koalas live in the eucalyptus forests of eastern Australia. Though it is often called a koala ______ koala is not a bear at all. It is a marsupial, meaning that its young develop in a pouch. Koalas eat almost nothing but eucalyptus leaves, which are low in nutrients and toxic to most animals. To save energy, they sleep for up to 20 hours a day.
qs.exp: "Though" already signals contrast; the dependent clause needs only a comma. Adding "however" is redundant and ungrammatical.
qs.mk: «Though»[d|it is often called a koala bear]⟨,⟩ [1|the koala is not a bear at all].

qs.passage: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived. Though it can grow to about 30 meters long, it feeds almost entirely on krill, tiny shrimp-like animals. A single blue whale can eat several tons of krill a day. How such a huge animal finds enough food in the vast ocean was long a mystery. Recent ______ though, suggest that blue whales remember the locations of past feeding grounds.
qs.exp: Note the two uses: "Though it can grow…," = conjunction; "Recent studies, though, suggest" = adverb interrupting subject and verb → needs commas on both sides.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Recent studies]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|suggest] [d:noun clause|that blue whales remember the locations of past feeding grounds].

qs.passage: Polynesian navigators settled islands across a vast area of the Pacific Ocean, from Hawaii to New Zealand. They traveled in double-hulled canoes, guided by the stars, ocean swells, and the flight paths of birds. The sweet potato, which originated in South America, was being grown in Polynesia centuries before Europeans arrived. Genetic studies suggest that Polynesians and Native South Americans met around 1200 ______ exactly where and how they met remains uncertain. Some researchers think that South Americans may have sailed west instead.
qs.exp: "Though" here is a conjunction; a dash (or comma) can attach its clause. A semicolon, period, or colon leaves "though…" as a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|Genetic studies suggest that Polynesians and Native South Americans met around 1200 CE]⟨—⟩«though»[d|exactly where and how they met remains uncertain].

qs.passage: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the tallest mountain in Africa. Although it lies just south of the equator, its summit has been capped with ice for thousands of years. That ice is disappearing ______ than 80 percent of the mountain's ice has vanished since 1912. Scientists estimate that the remaining glaciers could be gone within a few decades. Rising temperatures and drier air are both thought to play a role.
qs.exp: ", though." ends a sentence (though = however); a new sentence follows. ", though, more" = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|That ice is disappearing quickly]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|More than 80 percent of the mountain's ice has vanished since 1912].

qs.passage: Mercury orbits closer to the sun than any other planet. Its daytime temperatures can reach about 430°C. Nevertheless, Mercury is not the hottest ______ even though it is the closest to the sun. That title belongs to Venus, whose thick atmosphere traps heat. Because Mercury has almost no atmosphere, its nighttime temperatures plunge to about –180°C.
qs.exp: "Even though" clause after the main clause: comma OK; a period, semicolon, or colon creates a fragment.
qs.mk: {Nevertheless}, [1|Mercury is not the hottest planet]⟨,⟩ «even though»[d|it is the closest to the sun].

qs.passage: For decades, most scientists doubted that plants could communicate. In recent ______ studies have shown that some plants release chemicals that warn their neighbors of insect attacks. When caterpillars chew on certain plants, the plants release airborne chemicals. Nearby plants detect these signals and begin producing substances that make their leaves less tasty. Some researchers describe this as a kind of plant communication, though others prefer more cautious terms.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) follows the introductory phrase inside one clause: pair of commas. Compare the last sentence, where ", though others prefer…" uses "though" as a conjunction.
qs.mk: [p|In recent years]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1|studies have shown] [d:noun clause|that some plants release chemicals that warn their neighbors of insect attacks].

qs.passage: The heart beats roughly 100,000 times each day. Though only about the size of a ______ it pumps around 7,000 liters of blood through the body daily. Blood travels through a network of vessels that would stretch about 100,000 kilometers if laid end to end. That is long enough to circle Earth more than twice. The heart's steady rhythm is controlled by electrical signals from a small cluster of cells called the sinoatrial node.
qs.exp: "Though only about the size of a fist" is a shortened dependent clause; follow it with a comma.
qs.mk: «Though»[d:shortened clause|only about the size of a fist]⟨,⟩ [1|it pumps around 7,000 liters of blood through the body daily].

qs.passage: Chili peppers get their heat from a compound called capsaicin. Eating a hot pepper can make the mouth feel as if it is on fire. No real damage occurs in most ______ simply triggers the same nerve receptors that respond to actual heat. Birds, which spread pepper seeds, lack these receptors. As a result, they can eat even the hottest peppers without discomfort.
qs.exp: ", though." ends the sentence; a new sentence begins. ", though, capsaicin…" = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|No real damage occurs in most cases]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨.⟩ [2|Capsaicin simply triggers the same nerve receptors that respond to actual heat].

qs.passage: A desert is defined by how little precipitation it receives, not by its temperature. Many people picture deserts as places of burning sand and blazing sun. Though many deserts are ______ some, like the Gobi Desert in Asia, are bitterly cold in winter. Temperatures in the Gobi can drop below –40°C. Snow sometimes covers its dunes.
qs.exp: "Though" (conjunction) clause + comma + main clause.
qs.mk: «Though»[d|many deserts are hot]⟨,⟩ [1|some, like the Gobi Desert in Asia, are bitterly cold in winter].

qs.passage: On a clear night, most stars appear white to the naked eye. Viewed through a ______ stars display a range of colors from deep red to bright blue. A star's color reveals its surface temperature. Red stars are the coolest, while blue stars are the hottest. Our sun, a yellowish star, falls somewhere in the middle.
qs.exp: "Though" (= however) follows the introductory phrase and needs commas on both sides. Never use "however" and "though" together.
qs.mk: [p:intro phrase|Viewed through a telescope]⟨,⟩ {though}⟨,⟩ [1|stars display a range of colors from deep red to bright blue].

qs.passage: Penguins are usually associated with ice and snow. In fact, many penguin species live in temperate climates in South America, Africa, Australia, and New Zealand. Penguins are found almost entirely in the Southern ______ though one species, the Galápagos penguin, lives near the equator. Cool ocean currents bring cold, nutrient-rich water to the Galápagos Islands, allowing the penguins to survive there. No penguins live naturally in the Arctic.
qs.exp: "Though" (conjunction) clause after the main clause: comma. Other marks create a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|Penguins are found almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere]⟨,⟩ «though»[d|one species, the Galápagos penguin, lives near the equator].

label: Comma + FANBOYS ｜ 逗號＋對等連接詞

qs.passage: Bees are often credited with pollinating most of the world's crops. Flies, beetles, and moths also play important ______ some plants depend on them almost entirely. The cacao tree, the source of chocolate, is pollinated mainly by tiny midges. Without these insects, cacao farms would produce very little fruit. Protecting the damp, shady habitats that midges need is therefore a priority for many growers.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses joined by a FANBOYS conjunction need a comma BEFORE the conjunction. A comma alone = comma splice; no comma = run-on.
qs.mk: [1|Flies, beetles, and moths also play important roles]⟨,⟩ ‹and› [2|some plants depend on them almost entirely].

qs.passage: Venus is nearly the same size as Earth and is sometimes called Earth's twin. The two planets share a similar size and rocky ______ conditions on their surfaces could hardly be more different. Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps so much heat that surface temperatures reach about 465°C. Its air pressure is roughly 90 times that of Earth at sea level. Soviet landers that reached the surface in the 1970s and 1980s survived for about two hours at most.
qs.exp: ", but" correctly joins two independent clauses. ", however," between two clauses is a comma splice—"however" is an adverb, not a conjunction.
qs.mk: [1|The two planets share a similar size and rocky composition]⟨,⟩ ‹but› [2|conditions on their surfaces could hardly be more different].

qs.passage: Lightning heats the air around it to about 30,000°C in a fraction of a second. That is roughly five times hotter than the surface of the sun. The heated air expands ______ it produces a powerful shock wave that we hear as thunder. Because light travels much faster than sound, we see a flash before we hear the thunder. Counting the seconds between the two can help estimate how far away a storm is.
qs.exp: ", so" correctly joins two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice; never put a comma after "so" here.
qs.mk: [1|The heated air expands explosively]⟨,⟩ ‹so› [2|it produces a powerful shock wave] [d|that we hear as thunder].

qs.passage: Hummingbirds have the highest metabolism of any warm-blooded animal. Their hearts can beat more than 1,200 times per minute during flight. Ruby-throated hummingbirds weigh only about three ______ many of them fly nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico, a journey of about 800 kilometers. To prepare, the birds nearly double their body weight by storing fat. Researchers are still studying how such tiny animals navigate so accurately.
qs.exp: ", yet" (FANBOYS) joins two independent clauses with contrast. No comma after "yet."
qs.mk: [1|Ruby-throated hummingbirds weigh only about three grams]⟨,⟩ ‹yet› [2|many of them fly nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico][p:appositive|, a journey of about 800 kilometers].

qs.passage: Paper money first appeared in China during the Tang dynasty and became widespread under the Song dynasty. Merchants found heavy strings of copper coins inconvenient for large ______ they began depositing coins with trusted shops in exchange for paper receipts. Over time, the government took control of issuing these notes. When Marco Polo visited China in the late 1200s, he was amazed that paper could be used as money. Europe would not widely adopt paper currency for several more centuries.
qs.exp: ", so" joins two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Merchants found heavy strings of copper coins inconvenient for large transactions]⟨,⟩ ‹so› [2|they began depositing coins with trusted shops in exchange for paper receipts].

qs.passage: The ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia, Greece, for more than a thousand years. In the 1890s, the French educator Pierre de Coubertin proposed reviving the tradition. The first modern Games took place in Athens in 1896. About 240 athletes from 14 nations ______ none of them were women. Women first competed four years later, at the 1900 Games in Paris.
qs.exp: ", but" joins two independent clauses. ", however" between clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|About 240 athletes from 14 nations competed]⟨,⟩ ‹but› [2|none of them were women].

qs.passage: Visitors to Iceland can explore glaciers, volcanoes, and black-sand beaches. Many travelers come in winter hoping to see the northern ______ they visit in summer to experience the midnight sun. In June, the sun barely sets in the northern part of the country. In December, by contrast, daylight in Reykjavík lasts only about four hours. Each season offers a very different experience of the island.
qs.exp: ", or" joins two independent clauses. No comma after the conjunction; a semicolon before "or" is not standard.
qs.mk: [1|Many travelers come in winter hoping to see the northern lights]⟨,⟩ ‹or› [2|they visit in summer to experience the midnight sun].

qs.passage: The ostrich is the largest living bird, standing up to 2.7 meters tall. Its wings are far too small to lift its heavy body off the ground. The bird has long, powerful ______ it can outrun most of its predators, reaching speeds of about 70 kilometers per hour. Each foot has only two toes, an adaptation that helps with speed. When cornered, an ostrich can deliver a kick strong enough to injure a lion.
qs.exp: ", so" joins two clauses. "Therefore" is an adverb, so ", therefore" between clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The bird has long, powerful legs]⟨,⟩ ‹so› [2|it can outrun most of its predators][p|, reaching speeds of about 70 kilometers per hour].

qs.passage: Pompeii was a busy Roman city near the Bay of Naples. In 79 CE, nearby Mount Vesuvius ______ ash and pumice buried the city within hours. The ash preserved buildings, paintings, and even loaves of bread. Archaeologists later poured plaster into hollow spaces left by victims' bodies, creating detailed casts. Today, Pompeii is one of the most visited archaeological sites in the world.
qs.exp: ", and" joins two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice.
qs.mk: [p|In 79 CE,] [1|nearby Mount Vesuvius erupted]⟨,⟩ ‹and› [2|ash and pumice buried the city within hours].

qs.passage: Hardness measures how well a material resists scratching. On the Mohs scale, diamonds rank 10, the highest possible score. Diamonds are the hardest natural ______ they can shatter if struck sharply at the right angle. This is because hardness and toughness are different properties. Jade, for example, is much softer than diamond but far more resistant to breaking.
qs.exp: ", yet" joins two independent clauses. ", though," (adverb) between two clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Diamonds are the hardest natural material]⟨,⟩ ‹yet› [2|they can shatter] [d|if struck sharply at the right angle].

qs.passage: The Netherlands is one of the flattest countries in the world. About a quarter of its land lies below sea ______ the Dutch have built an extensive system of dikes, dams, and storm barriers to keep the water out. Windmills were once used to pump water from low-lying fields. Today, electric pumps do most of this work. The country's expertise in water management is now sought by cities around the world.
qs.exp: ", so" joins two clauses. "Thus" is an adverb, so ", thus" between clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|About a quarter of its land lies below sea level]⟨,⟩ ‹so› [2|the Dutch have built an extensive system of dikes, dams, and storm barriers to keep the water out].

qs.passage: For astronomers, Earth's atmosphere is a nuisance because it blurs and distorts starlight. Placing a telescope in orbit avoids this problem. The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in ______ its first images were disappointingly blurry because its main mirror had been ground to the wrong shape. In 1993, astronauts installed corrective optics during a spacewalk mission. Since then, Hubble has produced some of the most famous images in the history of astronomy.
qs.exp: ", but" joins two clauses. ", however" between clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The Hubble Space Telescope was launched in 1990]⟨,⟩ ‹but› [2|its first images were disappointingly blurry] «because»[d|its main mirror had been ground to the wrong shape].

qs.passage: Chess is believed to have originated in India around the sixth century CE. The early game, called chaturanga, represented four divisions of an army. Chess spread to Persia and later to ______ its rules changed along the way. The queen, once one of the weakest pieces, became the most powerful in the late 1400s. This change made the game much faster.
qs.exp: ", and" joins two independent clauses. A comma alone = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Chess spread to Persia and later to Europe]⟨,⟩ ‹and› [2|its rules changed along the way].

qs.passage: Japan's first high-speed rail line opened in 1964, just before the Tokyo Olympics. Its trains are famous for their speed and punctuality. Travelers going from Tokyo to Osaka can take the train, which takes about two and a half ______ they can take a short flight, which requires extra time for airport security. Many travelers prefer the train because stations are located in city centers. The average delay on the line is measured in seconds rather than minutes.
qs.exp: ", or" joins two independent clauses. "Otherwise" is an adverb → comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Travelers going from Tokyo to Osaka can take the train, which takes about two and a half hours]⟨,⟩ ‹or› [2|they can take a short flight, which requires extra time for airport security].

qs.passage: Saturn is the second-largest planet in the solar ______ it is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub of water. Saturn's average density is less than that of water because it is made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Its famous rings are made of countless pieces of ice and rock. Some pieces are as small as grains of sand, while others are as large as houses. Galileo first observed the rings in 1610, but his telescope was too weak to show their shape clearly.
qs.exp: ", yet" joins two clauses. ", nevertheless" (adverb) = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Saturn is the second-largest planet in the solar system]⟨,⟩ ‹yet› [2|it is so light for its size that it would float in a giant bathtub of water].

qs.passage: The Perseverance rover landed on Mars in February ______ it carried a small helicopter named Ingenuity. Ingenuity was designed to make up to five test flights over about a month. Flying on Mars is difficult because the planet's atmosphere is only about 1 percent as dense as Earth's. Ingenuity exceeded all expectations and made 72 flights before a damaged rotor ended its mission in 2024. Its success has encouraged engineers to design larger helicopters for future missions.
qs.exp: ", and" joins two clauses. A comma alone = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The Perseverance rover landed on Mars in February 2021]⟨,⟩ ‹and› [2|it carried a small helicopter named Ingenuity].

qs.passage: Botanists define a fruit as the part of a plant that develops from a flower and contains seeds. By this definition, tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers are all fruits. Tomatoes are botanically ______ the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in 1893 that they should be taxed as vegetables. The case, Nix v. Hedden, turned on how ordinary people used the word, not on science. Most cooks still treat tomatoes as vegetables because they are usually eaten in savory dishes.
qs.exp: ", but" joins two clauses. A comma alone = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Tomatoes are botanically fruits]⟨,⟩ ‹but› [2|the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in 1893] [d:noun clause|that they should be taxed as vegetables].

qs.passage: Archerfish live in mangrove swamps and rivers in Southeast Asia and northern Australia. They have an unusual hunting technique. An archerfish spots an insect resting on a leaf above the ______ shoots it down with a powerful jet of water from its mouth. The fish can adjust for the way light bends at the water's surface. Some can hit targets more than a meter away.
qs.exp: "Spots… and shoots…" is ONE subject with two verbs (compound predicate), so no comma before "and." Use ", and" only between two independent clauses.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|An archerfish] [1:Verb 1|spots an insect resting on a leaf above the water] ⟨∅⟩‹and› [1:Verb 2|shoots it down with a powerful jet of water from its mouth].

qs.passage: Fireflies are beetles that produce light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens. The light is extremely efficient, giving off almost no heat. Each species has its own distinctive pattern of ______ females can recognize males of their own kind. Some predatory fireflies imitate the flashes of other species to lure males and eat them. Light pollution can interfere with these signals and make it harder for fireflies to find mates.
qs.exp: ", so" joins two clauses. ", therefore" = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Each species has its own distinctive pattern of flashes]⟨,⟩ ‹so› [2|females can recognize males of their own kind].

qs.passage: Sunflowers are often said to follow the sun across the sky. Young sunflowers do turn from east to west during the ______ mature flowers usually face east all day. Researchers found that east-facing flower heads warm up faster in the morning. Warm flowers attract more bees and other pollinators. This simple behavior may therefore help sunflowers reproduce.
qs.exp: ", but" alone joins the clauses. "but however" is redundant; ", however" = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Young sunflowers do turn from east to west during the day]⟨,⟩ ‹but› [2|mature flowers usually face east all day].

qs.passage: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world. Some parts of it receive almost no rain for years at a time. The region is extremely ______ it sits above some of the largest underground water reserves on Earth. Much of this water, called fossil water, fell as rain thousands of years ago when the region was much wetter. Because it is not replaced quickly, pumping it out faster than it refills could exhaust the supply.
qs.exp: ", yet" joins two clauses. ", however" = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The region is extremely dry]⟨,⟩ ‹yet› [2|it sits above some of the largest underground water reserves on Earth].

label: Subordinating conjunction (because, while, unless…) ｜ 從屬連接詞

qs.passage: Sea otters spend nearly their entire lives in cold Pacific waters. Unlike whales and seals, they have no thick layer of blubber to keep them warm. Instead, they rely on extremely dense fur, which traps a layer of air against their skin. They must also eat about a quarter of their body weight in food each ______ their high metabolism burns energy quickly to generate heat. By keeping sea urchin populations in check, otters help kelp forests thrive.
qs.exp: A "because" clause that follows the main clause needs no punctuation. A period or semicolon leaves "Because…" as a fragment; a comma AFTER "because" is never correct.
qs.mk: [1|They must also eat about a quarter of their body weight in food each day] ⟨∅⟩«because»[d|their high metabolism burns energy quickly to generate heat].

qs.passage: Alligators and crocodiles are often confused with each other. Both are large reptiles with powerful jaws and armored skin. An alligator has a broad, U-shaped ______ a crocodile has a narrower, V-shaped one. When a crocodile closes its mouth, its large fourth lower tooth remains visible. Alligators, by contrast, tend to hide their lower teeth when their jaws are shut.
qs.exp: "Whereas" is a subordinating conjunction; ", whereas" attaches its clause to the main clause. A period or semicolon before it leaves a fragment; a comma after it is wrong.
qs.mk: [1|An alligator has a broad, U-shaped snout]⟨,⟩ «whereas»[d|a crocodile has a narrower, V-shaped one].

qs.passage: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest structure built by living things on Earth, stretching more than 2,000 kilometers along Australia's coast. It is made up of nearly 3,000 individual reefs and hundreds of islands. Remarkably, the reef is large enough to be seen from ______ it was built by coral polyps, tiny animals that are often only a few millimeters across. Over thousands of years, the polyps' limestone skeletons accumulated into massive structures. Today, the reef is home to about 1,500 species of fish.
qs.exp: "Even though" introduces a dependent clause that can follow the main clause after a comma. ", however," is a comma splice; a semicolon or period before "Even though" leaves a fragment.
qs.mk: {Remarkably}, [1|the reef is large enough to be seen from space]⟨,⟩ «even though»[d|it was built by coral polyps][p:appositive|, tiny animals that are often only a few millimeters across].

qs.passage: Many hospitals now use ultraviolet robots to disinfect rooms. The devices emit UV-C light, which damages the genetic material of bacteria and viruses. The light works only on surfaces that it can reach directly. Shadowed areas remain ______ the robot is moved to a new position. Hospital staff therefore still clean rooms by hand before using the robots.
qs.exp: An "unless" clause following the main clause needs no punctuation. A period or semicolon creates a fragment; never place a comma after "unless."
qs.mk: [1|Shadowed areas remain contaminated] ⟨∅⟩«unless»[d|the robot is moved to a new position].

qs.passage: Washington, D.C., is famous for its cherry blossoms. The city's first cherry trees were planted in ______ the mayor of Tokyo sent more than 3,000 of them as a gift of friendship. An earlier shipment in 1910 had to be destroyed because the trees were infested with insects. Today, the blossoms attract more than a million visitors each spring. The peak bloom usually occurs in late March or early April.
qs.exp: "After" introduces a dependent clause attached to the main clause. A period or semicolon creates a fragment; no comma after "after."
qs.mk: [1|The city's first cherry trees were planted in 1912]⟨,⟩ «after»[d|the mayor of Tokyo sent more than 3,000 of them as a gift of friendship].

qs.passage: The Great Fire of London began in a bakery on Pudding Lane in September 1666. Over four days, it destroyed more than 13,000 houses and nearly 90 churches. The fire spread ______ most buildings were made of timber and packed tightly together. Afterward, the city was rebuilt with wider streets and buildings of brick and stone. The architect Christopher Wren designed a new St. Paul's Cathedral, which was completed in 1711.
qs.exp: A "because" clause after the main clause needs no punctuation. A period/semicolon creates a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|The fire spread quickly] ⟨∅⟩«because»[d|most buildings were made of timber and packed tightly together].

qs.passage: Earth's North and South Poles are both cold, but they differ in important ways. The North Pole sits on floating sea ice in the middle of the Arctic ______ the South Pole lies on a thick ice sheet covering solid land. Because of its higher elevation, the South Pole is much colder. Its average annual temperature is about –49°C, compared with about –18°C at the North Pole. Polar bears live only in the Arctic, and penguins live mainly in the Southern Hemisphere.
qs.exp: ", while" (contrast) attaches a dependent clause to the main clause. A semicolon or period before "while" creates a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|The North Pole sits on floating sea ice in the middle of the Arctic Ocean]⟨,⟩ «while»[d|the South Pole lies on a thick ice sheet covering solid land].

qs.passage: Sloths are famous for moving slowly, and their low metabolism lets them survive on a diet of leaves. Although these animals spend most of their lives hanging in ______ they climb down to the ground about once a week to relieve themselves. The trip is dangerous because sloths are slow and vulnerable on the ground. Scientists are still debating why sloths take this risk. One hypothesis suggests that the behavior helps support moths and algae that live in sloth fur.
qs.exp: "Although" already shows contrast; it needs only a comma before the main clause. Adding "however" is redundant and creates a fragment or comma splice.
qs.mk: «Although»[d|these animals spend most of their lives hanging in trees]⟨,⟩ [1|they climb down to the ground about once a week to relieve themselves].

qs.passage: Living in space changes the human body in many ways. Without gravity pulling on them, muscles and bones no longer work to support the body's weight. Astronauts on the International Space Station exercise about two hours every ______ their muscles and bones do not weaken too much. Even so, some astronauts lose bone density during long missions. After returning to Earth, they may need weeks or months of rehabilitation to walk normally again.
qs.exp: "So that" (purpose) introduces a dependent clause; no comma is needed. A period or semicolon creates a fragment; never a comma after "that."
qs.mk: [1|Astronauts on the International Space Station exercise about two hours every day] ⟨∅⟩«so that»[d|their muscles and bones do not weaken too much].

qs.passage: Emperor penguins breed during the Antarctic winter, when temperatures can fall below –40°C. While most birds build nests in trees or on the ______ emperor penguins build no nests at all. Instead, the male balances the single egg on his feet and covers it with a warm fold of skin. He then goes without food for about two months while the egg incubates. Males huddle together in large groups, taking turns on the cold outer edge.
qs.exp: Introductory "While" clause + comma. Adding "however" is redundant; a period or semicolon creates a fragment.
qs.mk: «While»[d|most birds build nests in trees or on the ground]⟨,⟩ [1|emperor penguins build no nests at all].

qs.passage: Chameleons are lizards known for their ability to change color. Many people assume that they do so mainly to match their ______ although camouflage is only part of the story. Chameleons also change color to regulate body temperature and to signal to other chameleons. A male may turn bright colors to warn rivals or attract a mate. The color change is controlled by tiny crystals in skin cells that reflect light differently as they move closer together or farther apart.
qs.exp: "Although" introduces a dependent clause; attach it with a comma. Stronger marks leave a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|Many people assume that they do so mainly to match their surroundings]⟨,⟩ «although»[d|camouflage is only part of the story].

qs.passage: Owls are skilled nighttime hunters. They have excellent hearing and can locate prey in total darkness. Many owls can also fly almost ______ the edges of their wing feathers are soft and fringed, which breaks up the air turbulence that creates noise. Engineers have studied owl feathers to design quieter fans and wind turbines. Some owls' ears are placed at different heights on their heads, helping them pinpoint sounds.
qs.exp: "Because" clause after the main clause: no punctuation needed. ", because of this," between two clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Many owls can also fly almost silently] ⟨∅⟩«because»[d|the edges of their wing feathers are soft and fringed, which breaks up the air turbulence that creates noise].

qs.passage: Deciduous trees lose their leaves each autumn. Before the leaves fall, they often turn brilliant shades of yellow, orange, and red. The change ______ shorter days cause the trees to stop producing chlorophyll, the green pigment used in photosynthesis. As the chlorophyll breaks down, other pigments that were present all along become visible. Red colors, however, come from new pigments that some trees produce in the fall.
qs.exp: "When" clause after the verb completes the sentence; no punctuation. A period/semicolon creates fragments.
qs.mk: [1|The change begins] ⟨∅⟩«when»[d|shorter days cause the trees to stop producing chlorophyll][p:appositive|, the green pigment used in photosynthesis].

qs.passage: Pacific salmon hatch in freshwater streams and soon migrate to the ocean. They spend several years growing in the open ______ they return to the very stream where they hatched to spawn. Scientists believe that salmon use Earth's magnetic field to find the right stretch of coast. Once near their home river, they follow its distinctive smell upstream. Most Pacific salmon die soon after spawning, and their bodies provide nutrients to the surrounding forest.
qs.exp: "Before" clause after the main clause: no punctuation. A period/semicolon creates a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|They spend several years growing in the open ocean] ⟨∅⟩«before»[d|they return to the very stream where they hatched to spawn].

label: Comma after introductory clause/phrase ｜ 前置從屬子句/片語後加逗號

qs.passage: The platypus, which lives in the rivers of eastern Australia, has puzzled scientists since the 1790s. When the first preserved specimen reached Britain, some researchers suspected it was a hoax. The animal has a duck-like bill, a beaver-like tail, and webbed feet, and it lays eggs. Although the platypus is a ______ it has no nipples. Females instead release milk through patches of skin on their bellies, and the young lap it up.
qs.exp: An introductory "Although" clause is followed by a comma before the main clause. A semicolon or period would create a fragment.
qs.mk: «Although»[d|the platypus is a mammal]⟨,⟩ [1|it has no nipples].

qs.passage: The Amazon River flows about 6,400 kilometers across South America before reaching the Atlantic Ocean. It discharges more water than any other river on Earth. Even though it is one of the world's most important ______ no bridge crosses the Amazon anywhere along its main channel. Much of the river runs through sparsely populated rainforest, where roads are few. In addition, its banks are soft and shift frequently during the rainy season.
qs.exp: An introductory "Even though" clause ends with a comma before the main clause. Any stronger mark leaves the dependent clause as a fragment.
qs.mk: «Even though»[d|it is one of the world's most important rivers]⟨,⟩ [1|no bridge crosses the Amazon anywhere along its main channel].

qs.passage: Arctic ground squirrels hibernate for up to eight months each year. During hibernation, their body temperature can drop below the freezing point of water. When a squirrel wakes briefly every few ______ its body temperature rapidly climbs back to about 36°C. Scientists are not sure why the animals undergo these costly warm-ups. One hypothesis is that the periods of warmth allow the brain to repair itself.
qs.exp: An introductory "When" clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.
qs.mk: «When»[d|a squirrel wakes briefly every few weeks]⟨,⟩ [1|its body temperature rapidly climbs back to about 36°C].

qs.passage: Frogs live on every continent except Antarctica. Their life cycle usually begins with a cluster of jelly-coated eggs. While most frogs lay their eggs in ______ some species have developed very different strategies. The male Darwin's frog, for example, carries tadpoles in his vocal sac until they become tiny froglets. Such adaptations protect the young from predators and from ponds that may dry up.
qs.exp: An introductory "While" clause is followed by a comma. Other marks leave the dependent clause as a fragment.
qs.mk: «While»[d|most frogs lay their eggs in water]⟨,⟩ [1|some species have developed very different strategies].

qs.passage: The Dead Sea lies on the border between Jordan and the West Bank, more than 400 meters below sea level. Its shoreline is the lowest point of dry land on Earth. Because the lake is nearly ten times saltier than the ______ swimmers float on its surface with almost no effort. The high salt content also means that fish and plants cannot survive in its waters. Over the past several decades, the Dead Sea's surface has dropped by about one meter per year.
qs.exp: An introductory "Because" clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.
qs.mk: «Because»[d|the lake is nearly ten times saltier than the ocean]⟨,⟩ [1|swimmers float on its surface with almost no effort].

qs.passage: Before the 1450s, most books in Europe were copied by hand, often by monks. A single Bible could take a scribe more than a year to complete. Johannes Gutenberg's printing press, which used movable metal type, changed this dramatically. Since the invention of the printing ______ books have been produced in ever-increasing numbers. By 1500, presses across Europe had printed millions of copies of thousands of different titles.
qs.exp: A comma follows the long introductory phrase "Since the invention of the printing press."
qs.mk: [p:intro phrase|Since the invention of the printing press]⟨,⟩ [1|books have been produced in ever-increasing numbers].

qs.passage: Today, the Eiffel Tower is the most recognizable symbol of Paris. When it was completed in 1889, however, many Parisians considered it ugly. A group of artists and writers even signed a public letter protesting its construction. Built as a temporary entrance arch for a world's ______ the tower was supposed to be taken down after 20 years. It was saved partly because it proved useful as a radio transmission tower.
qs.exp: An introductory participial phrase ("Built as…") is followed by a comma before the subject.
qs.mk: [p:intro phrase|Built as a temporary entrance arch for a world's fair]⟨,⟩ [1|the tower was supposed to be taken down after 20 years].

qs.passage: About 20,000 years ago, vast ice sheets covered much of North America and northern Europe. So much water was locked in ice that sea levels were far lower than they are today. A land bridge called Beringia connected Siberia and Alaska. As the climate warmed at the end of the last Ice ______ melting glaciers raised sea levels by more than 100 meters. Beringia disappeared beneath the waves, separating Asia from North America.
qs.exp: An introductory "As" clause is followed by a comma.
qs.mk: «As»[d|the climate warmed at the end of the last Ice Age]⟨,⟩ [1|melting glaciers raised sea levels by more than 100 meters].

qs.passage: Greenland is the world's largest island, and about 80 percent of it is covered by ice. In some places, the ice sheet is more than three kilometers thick. If all of that ice were to ______ global sea levels would rise by about seven meters. Such a complete melt would take centuries or longer. Even so, the ice sheet is currently losing hundreds of billions of tons of ice each year.
qs.exp: An introductory "If" clause is followed by a comma.
qs.mk: «If»[d|all of that ice were to melt]⟨,⟩ [1|global sea levels would rise by about seven meters].

qs.passage: Octopuses are notorious escape artists in aquariums. One octopus in New Zealand famously slipped out of its tank and made its way down a drainpipe to the sea. Since octopuses have no ______ they can squeeze through any opening larger than their hard beak. Their soft bodies also let them hide in narrow cracks in rocks. Aquarium staff often have to secure tank lids with locks or weights.
qs.exp: An introductory "Since" (= because) clause is followed by a comma.
qs.mk: «Since»[d|octopuses have no bones]⟨,⟩ [1|they can squeeze through any opening larger than their hard beak].

qs.passage: Camels are well suited to life in the desert. Contrary to popular belief, a camel's hump does not hold water. To survive long journeys without ______ camels store fat in their humps, which they can break down for energy. They can also drink more than 100 liters of water in just a few minutes. Their oval red blood cells keep flowing even when the camel is dehydrated.
qs.exp: An introductory infinitive phrase ("To survive…") is followed by a comma.
qs.mk: [p:intro phrase|To survive long journeys without food]⟨,⟩ [1|camels store fat in their humps]⟨,⟩ [d:nonessential|which they can break down for energy].

qs.passage: Octopuses differ from other animals in many surprising ways. Unlike humans and most other ______ they have three hearts. Two of the hearts pump blood through the gills, while the third pumps it to the rest of the body. Their blood is blue because it contains a copper-based protein called hemocyanin. This protein carries oxygen efficiently in cold water with little oxygen.
qs.exp: An introductory "Unlike…" phrase is followed by a comma.
qs.mk: [p:intro phrase|Unlike humans and most other animals]⟨,⟩ [1|they have three hearts].

label: Semicolon between independent clauses ｜ 分號連接兩獨立子句

qs.passage: Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. They support roughly a quarter of all known marine ______ many of these species are found nowhere else. Reefs also protect coastlines and support fishing and tourism industries. Rising ocean temperatures, however, threaten their survival. When water becomes too warm, corals expel the algae that live in their tissues and turn white.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses with no conjunction need a semicolon (or period). A comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on; "which" makes the sentence ungrammatical.
qs.mk: [1|They support roughly a quarter of all known marine species]⟨;⟩ [2|many of these species are found nowhere else].

qs.passage: Rubber trees are native to the Amazon rainforest. In the nineteenth century, demand for rubber soared as factories began producing tires, hoses, and waterproof clothing. In 1876, the British explorer Henry Wickham shipped about 70,000 rubber tree seeds from Brazil to ______ seedlings grown from them were later sent to British colonies in Asia. Within a few decades, plantations in Southeast Asia dominated the world's rubber supply. Brazil's rubber boom, meanwhile, collapsed.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses with no conjunction need a semicolon. Comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on.
qs.mk: [p|In 1876,] [1|the British explorer Henry Wickham shipped about 70,000 rubber tree seeds from Brazil to London]⟨;⟩ [2|seedlings grown from them were later sent to British colonies in Asia].

qs.passage: The violin family includes four main instruments: the violin, the viola, the cello, and the double bass. The cello is played sitting down, with the instrument resting between the player's knees. The double bass is even ______ is often taller than the musician playing it. Its deep notes provide the foundation of an orchestra's sound. Jazz musicians frequently pluck the bass instead of using a bow.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses, no conjunction → semicolon. Comma = comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The double bass is even larger]⟨;⟩ [2|it is often taller than the musician playing it].

qs.passage: The Titanic was the largest ship afloat when it set out on its first voyage in April 1912. Four days into the trip, it struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic. The ship carried lifeboats for only about half of the people on ______ more than 1,500 people died when it sank. The disaster led to new international rules requiring enough lifeboat space for everyone on board. It also led to the creation of an ice patrol to track icebergs in shipping lanes.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses, no conjunction → semicolon.
qs.mk: [1|The ship carried lifeboats for only about half of the people on board]⟨;⟩ [2|more than 1,500 people died] «when»[d|it sank].

qs.passage: The first vaccine was developed by Edward Jenner in 1796. Jenner noticed that milkmaids who had caught cowpox seemed protected from ______ this observation led him to test the idea on a young boy. He infected the boy with cowpox and later exposed him to smallpox, and the boy did not become ill. The word vaccine comes from vacca, the Latin word for cow. Smallpox was declared eradicated worldwide in 1980.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses, no conjunction → semicolon.
qs.mk: [1|Jenner noticed that milkmaids who had caught cowpox seemed protected from smallpox]⟨;⟩ [2|this observation led him to test the idea on a young boy].

qs.passage: Venus is unusual in several ways. It rotates very slowly, taking about 243 Earth days to spin once on its axis. It also spins in the opposite direction from most ______ on Venus, the sun rises in the west and sets in the east. A day on Venus is therefore longer than its year, which lasts about 225 Earth days. Scientists are not sure why Venus spins backward.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses, no conjunction → semicolon.
qs.mk: [1|It also spins in the opposite direction from most planets]⟨;⟩ [2|on Venus, the sun rises in the west and sets in the east].

qs.passage: The Venus flytrap is one of the few plants that can move quickly. It grows naturally in only one small region of the ______ is found in wetlands within about 100 kilometers of Wilmington, North Carolina. Its leaves snap shut when an insect touches tiny trigger hairs inside them twice within about 20 seconds. This double-touch system prevents the plant from wasting energy on raindrops or falling debris. Once the trap closes, the plant releases digestive juices that dissolve the insect over several days.
qs.exp: Two independent clauses, no conjunction → semicolon.
qs.mk: [1|It grows naturally in only one small region of the world]⟨;⟩ [2|it is found in wetlands within about 100 kilometers of Wilmington, North Carolina].

label: Sentence boundary: period / run-on / comma splice ｜ 句子界線

qs.passage: Sourdough bread is made with a starter, a mixture of flour and water that contains wild yeast and bacteria. Bakers keep their starters alive by feeding them fresh flour regularly. Some bakeries claim that their starters are more than a century ______ microbes in a starter produce gases that make dough rise and acids that give the bread its tangy flavor. Scientists studying starters from around the world have found surprising diversity in the microbes they contain.
qs.exp: Two complete sentences must be separated by a period (or semicolon). Comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on; "Which" starts a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|Some bakeries claim that their starters are more than a century old]⟨.⟩ [2|The microbes in a starter produce gases that make dough rise and acids that give the bread its tangy flavor].

label: Other transition adverbs (therefore, instead…) ｜ 其他連接副詞

qs.passage: Many deserts receive less than 25 centimeters of rain a year. Plants in these environments must store water whenever it becomes available. The saguaro cactus has pleated stems that can expand like an accordion after a ______ a single large saguaro can absorb hundreds of liters of water in a day. This stored water allows the cactus to survive months of drought. Its waxy skin and spines further reduce water loss.
qs.exp: "In fact" is a transition that begins the second independent clause: semicolon before, comma after. A comma before it creates a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|The saguaro cactus has pleated stems that can expand like an accordion after a storm]⟨;⟩ {in fact}⟨,⟩ [2|a single large saguaro can absorb hundreds of liters of water in a day].

qs.passage: Penguins cannot fly, but they are superb swimmers. Their wings have evolved into stiff flippers that propel them through the water. Their bones are also denser than those of flying ______ the birds can dive deep without struggling against buoyancy. Emperor penguins have been recorded diving more than 500 meters below the surface. Some of their dives last over twenty minutes.
qs.exp: "Therefore" begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after. ", therefore," between clauses is a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Their bones are also denser than those of flying birds]⟨;⟩ {therefore}⟨,⟩ [2|the birds can dive deep without struggling against buoyancy].

qs.passage: Many animals use tools, a behavior once thought to be uniquely human. Chimpanzees strip leaves from twigs and use them to fish termites from their mounds. Birds can be skilled tool users as ______ New Caledonian crows shape twigs into hooked tools to pull insects out of tree bark. Some sea otters use rocks to crack open shellfish while floating on their backs. These examples suggest that tool use has evolved independently many times.
qs.exp: "For example" introduces a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|Birds can be skilled tool users as well]⟨;⟩ {for example}⟨,⟩ [2|New Caledonian crows shape twigs into hooked tools to pull insects out of tree bark].

qs.passage: The kakapo is a large, flightless parrot found only in New Zealand. Introduced predators such as cats and stoats nearly drove it to extinction. By 1995, only about 50 birds remained. The kakapo breeds slowly, and many of its eggs are ______ conservationists have steadily increased its population by moving the birds to predator-free islands. Today, more than 200 kakapo are alive.
qs.exp: "Nevertheless" (like "however") begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|The kakapo breeds slowly, and many of its eggs are infertile]⟨;⟩ {nevertheless}⟨,⟩ [2|conservationists have steadily increased its population by moving the birds to predator-free islands].

qs.passage: Vampire bats are the only mammals that feed entirely on blood. They live in Central and South America and usually feed on cattle, horses, and birds. Despite their reputation, vampire bats do not suck ______ they make a small cut with their sharp teeth and lap up the blood with their tongues. Their saliva contains a substance that keeps blood from clotting. Scientists have studied this substance, called draculin, as a possible medicine for stroke patients.
qs.exp: "Instead" begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [p|Despite their reputation,] [1|vampire bats do not suck blood]⟨;⟩ {instead}⟨,⟩ [2|they make a small cut with their sharp teeth and lap up the blood with their tongues].

qs.passage: Coffee plants grow best in a narrow range of temperatures. Rising global temperatures are making some traditional growing regions too ______ farmers in some countries are moving their coffee fields to higher, cooler elevations. Arabica coffee, which accounts for most of the world's production, is especially sensitive to heat. Researchers are also studying wild coffee species that may tolerate warmer conditions. One such species, Coffea stenophylla, was rediscovered in the wild in Sierra Leone in 2018.
qs.exp: "Consequently" begins a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|Rising global temperatures are making some traditional growing regions too hot]⟨;⟩ {consequently}⟨,⟩ [2|farmers in some countries are moving their coffee fields to higher, cooler elevations].

qs.passage: Walking is one of the simplest forms of exercise. It requires no special equipment, and most people can do it almost ______ studies link regular walking to lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, and depression. Even short walks after meals can help control blood sugar. Some researchers recommend aiming for about 7,000 to 10,000 steps a day. Walking with friends can add social benefits as well.
qs.exp: "Moreover" starts a new independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|It requires no special equipment, and most people can do it almost anywhere]⟨;⟩ {moreover}⟨,⟩ [2|studies link regular walking to lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, and depression].

qs.passage: Many common words in English come from other languages. The word ______ probably comes from a Hokkien Chinese word for a fermented fish sauce. Similarly, the word shampoo comes from Hindi, and the word robot comes from Czech. English has borrowed so freely that only a minority of its words come directly from Old English. These borrowed words reflect centuries of trade, conquest, and cultural exchange.
qs.exp: "For example" interrupts subject and verb: pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The word ketchup]⟨,⟩ {for example}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|probably comes from a Hokkien Chinese word for a fermented fish sauce].

qs.passage: Bamboo is technically a grass, not a tree. Some species can grow nearly a meter in a single ______ bamboo can be harvested far more often than timber from trees. Builders in Asia have used bamboo for scaffolding for centuries. The material is lightweight but has a tensile strength comparable to that of some steels. Bamboo is now being promoted as a sustainable building material.
qs.exp: Period + "As a result," starts a new sentence. A comma before it creates a comma splice.
qs.mk: [1|Some species can grow nearly a meter in a single day]⟨.⟩ {As a result}⟨,⟩ [2|bamboo can be harvested far more often than timber from trees].

qs.passage: Butterflies and moths belong to the same group of insects. Butterflies usually fly during the day and often have brightly colored wings. Most ______ are active at night and tend to have duller colors that help them hide. Their antennae also differ: butterfly antennae end in small clubs, while moth antennae are often feathery. There are exceptions, however, and some moths are as colorful as any butterfly.
qs.exp: "In contrast" interrupts subject and verb: pair of commas.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Most moths]⟨,⟩ {in contrast}⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|are active at night and tend to have duller colors that help them hide].

qs.passage: A popular story claims that educated Europeans in the 1400s believed the Earth was flat. In fact, scholars had known that the Earth was round since ancient Greek times. The experts who doubted Christopher Columbus's plan did not think the Earth was ______ they believed he had greatly underestimated the distance from Europe to Asia. They were right. Columbus survived only because the Americas lay between Europe and Asia.
qs.exp: "Instead" begins the second clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|The experts who doubted Christopher Columbus's plan did not think the Earth was flat]⟨;⟩ {instead}⟨,⟩ [2|they believed he had greatly underestimated the distance from Europe to Asia].

qs.passage: In the 1960s, the United States and the Soviet Union raced to land people on the Moon. The Soviet Union achieved many early firsts, including the first satellite and the first human in ______ the United States invested heavily in the Apollo program. In July 1969, Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon. In total, twelve astronauts walked on the lunar surface between 1969 and 1972. No one has returned since the final Apollo mission.
qs.exp: "Meanwhile" begins the second clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|The Soviet Union achieved many early firsts, including the first satellite and the first human in orbit]⟨;⟩ {meanwhile}⟨,⟩ [2|the United States invested heavily in the Apollo program].

qs.passage: Beavers are sometimes called ecosystem engineers. Using branches, mud, and stones, they build dams across streams. These dams slow the flow of ______ they help reduce flooding and erosion downstream. The ponds that form behind the dams provide habitats for fish, frogs, birds, and insects. In some regions, conservationists have reintroduced beavers to help restore damaged wetlands.
qs.exp: "Thus" begins the second independent clause: semicolon before, comma after.
qs.mk: [1|These dams slow the flow of water]⟨;⟩ {thus}⟨,⟩ [2|they help reduce flooding and erosion downstream].

label: Colon introducing an explanation ｜ 冒號引出說明

qs.passage: For centuries, sailors could measure latitude by observing the height of the sun or the North Star. Longitude was a much harder problem. The difficulty was fundamentally about ______ calculate longitude, a navigator needed to know the exact time at a home port while at sea. Pendulum clocks, however, lost accuracy on rolling ships. In the 1760s, the English clockmaker John Harrison finally built a marine timekeeper reliable enough for the task.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete independent clause introduces the explanation of "the difficulty." A comma creates a comma splice; no punctuation creates a run-on; "; and" is not a standard way to join clauses.
qs.mk: [1|The difficulty was fundamentally about time]⟨:⟩ [p:explanation|to calculate longitude,] [2|a navigator needed to know the exact time at a home port while at sea].

qs.passage: Many early photographs show people with stiff, serious expressions. This was not necessarily because people in the 1800s were unhappy. One reason was ______ cameras required subjects to hold still for long periods, and a smile is hard to keep steady. Another reason was cultural, since formal portraits were expected to look dignified. By the early twentieth century, faster cameras and changing fashions made smiling portraits common.
qs.exp: The colon follows a complete clause and introduces the explanation of what the "practical" reason was. A comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on.
qs.mk: [1|One reason was practical]⟨:⟩ [2|early cameras required subjects to hold still for long periods, and a smile is hard to keep steady].

qs.passage: Honey can last for thousands of years without spoiling. Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that were still edible. The reason is ______ contains very little water and is highly acidic, conditions in which most bacteria cannot survive. Bees also add an enzyme that produces small amounts of hydrogen peroxide, which further protects the honey. As long as it is sealed to keep out moisture, honey can be stored almost indefinitely.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation. Comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on.
