qs.mk: [1|The reason is chemical]⟨:⟩ [2|honey contains very little water and is highly acidic][p:appositive|, conditions in which most bacteria cannot survive].

qs.passage: Elephants that raid farms can destroy a season's crops in a single night. Traditional fences are expensive and often fail to stop them. Farmers in Kenya have found a creative ______ hang beehives on wires strung between fence posts. When an elephant bumps the wire, the hives swing and the bees swarm out. Elephants avoid bees, which can sting the sensitive skin around their eyes and trunks.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces what the alternative is. Comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on.
qs.mk: [1|Farmers in Kenya have found a creative alternative]⟨:⟩ [2|they hang beehives on wires strung between fence posts].

qs.passage: Most people throw away a cup or bowl once it breaks. The Japanese art of kintsugi treats broken pottery in an unusual ______ of hiding the cracks, artisans fill them with lacquer mixed with powdered gold. The repaired object often looks more striking than the original. The practice reflects the idea that damage and repair are part of an object's history. Kintsugi has inspired artists and designers around the world.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation of the "unusual way."
qs.mk: [1|The Japanese art of kintsugi treats broken pottery in an unusual way]⟨:⟩ [p|instead of hiding the cracks,] [2|artisans fill them with lacquer mixed with powdered gold].

qs.passage: Flamingos are wading birds found in parts of Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Young flamingos are covered in gray or white feathers. The adults' famous pink color is not ______ comes from pigments in the algae and tiny shrimp they eat. Flamingos in zoos may fade if their diet lacks these pigments. For this reason, zookeepers often add special supplements to the birds' food.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation. Comma = comma splice; "because" after a colon makes a fragment.
qs.mk: [1|The adults' famous pink color is not inherited]⟨:⟩ [2|it comes from pigments in the algae and tiny shrimp they eat].

qs.passage: Cuttlefish can change the color and pattern of their skin in less than a second. They use this ability to hide from predators and to communicate with one another. Yet experiments suggest that cuttlefish are colorblind. This raises a puzzling ______ can an animal match colors it cannot see? Some researchers think that light-sensitive proteins in the skin itself may help.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete clause can introduce a question that explains "a puzzling question."
qs.mk: [1|This raises a puzzling question]⟨:⟩ [2:question|how can an animal match colors it cannot see]?

qs.passage: The Statue of Liberty was not always green. When it was dedicated in 1886, it had the reddish-brown shine of a new penny. The change came from a natural ______ on the statue's surface reacted with air and water over about 30 years, forming a green layer called a patina. This patina actually protects the copper beneath it from further corrosion. For that reason, it has never been removed.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation of the "natural process."
qs.mk: [1|The change came from a natural process]⟨:⟩ [2|copper on the statue's surface reacted with air and water over about 30 years][p|, forming a green layer called a patina].

qs.passage: The giant panda lives in the mountain forests of central China. The animal presents biologists with a nutritional ______ has the digestive system of a meat eater but eats almost nothing except bamboo. Because its gut digests bamboo poorly, a panda must eat for up to 14 hours a day. Pandas also conserve energy by moving slowly and resting often. Their thyroid hormone levels are unusually low, which further reduces their energy needs.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation of the "puzzle."
qs.mk: [1|The animal presents biologists with a nutritional puzzle]⟨:⟩ [2|it has the digestive system of a meat eater but eats almost nothing except bamboo].

qs.passage: The first emoji were created in Japan in 1999 by designer Shigetaka Kurita. His goal was ______ wanted to help people convey emotions in short text messages. His original set of 176 small images included symbols for weather, food, and facial expressions. In 2016, the Museum of Modern Art in New York added the set to its collection. Today, thousands of emoji are used by billions of people around the world.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation.
qs.mk: [1|His goal was practical]⟨:⟩ [2|he wanted to help people convey emotions in short text messages].

qs.passage: Humans begin yawning even before birth. Many other animals, including dogs, snakes, and fish, yawn as well. Scientists have proposed many explanations for this behavior, but one idea has gained ______ may help cool the brain. A deep yawn draws in air and increases blood flow to the head. Studies have found that people yawn less often when the surrounding air is very hot.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation. "that yawning may help…" after a colon is not a complete clause.
qs.mk: [1|Scientists have proposed many explanations for this behavior, but one idea has gained support]⟨:⟩ [2|yawning may help cool the brain].

qs.passage: In 1999, NASA lost contact with the Mars Climate Orbiter as it approached the planet. The cause turned out to be a simple ______ engineering team used English units, while another used metric units. As a result, the spacecraft flew too close to Mars and was destroyed in its atmosphere. The mission had cost about 125 million dollars. The incident is now taught as a lesson in the importance of clear communication.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the explanation of the "error."
qs.mk: [1|The cause turned out to be a simple error]⟨:⟩ [2|one engineering team used English units, while another used metric units].

label: Colon introducing a list / item ｜ 冒號引出列舉

qs.passage: The James Webb Space Telescope observes the universe primarily in infrared light. This choice allows it to study objects that visible-light telescopes struggle to ______ newly forming stars hidden inside dust clouds, the atmospheres of distant planets, and the faint light of the earliest galaxies. To detect such weak signals, the telescope's instruments must be kept extremely cold. A tennis-court-sized sunshield blocks heat from the sun, Earth, and Moon. Behind it, some instruments operate at temperatures below –260°C.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete clause introduces a list. Never put a colon after "such as" or "including"; a semicolon cannot introduce a list.
qs.mk: [1|This choice allows it to study objects] [d|that visible-light telescopes struggle to see]⟨:⟩ [p:list|newly forming stars hidden inside dust clouds, the atmospheres of distant planets, and the faint light of the earliest galaxies].

qs.passage: Marie Curie remains the only person to have won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences. Her research focused on radioactivity, a term she helped popularize. Together with her husband, Pierre, she discovered two new ______ polonium and radium. Polonium was named after Poland, Marie's homeland. Curie's notebooks are still so radioactive that they are stored in lead-lined boxes.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete clause introduces the two specific elements. No colon after "including" or "such as"; a semicolon cannot introduce a list.
qs.mk: [p|Together with her husband, Pierre,] [1|she discovered two new elements]⟨:⟩ [p:list|polonium and radium].

qs.passage: Some of the most valuable spices in history came from tropical islands. In the 1600s, Dutch and English merchants fought bitterly over a small group of Indonesian islands known as the Banda Islands. These islands were then the world's only source of two prized ______ nutmeg and mace. Both spices come from the same tree, Myristica fragrans. In 1667, the Dutch gave up their claim to Manhattan partly in exchange for Run, one of the Banda Islands.
qs.exp: A colon after the complete clause introduces the two spices. No colon after "such as" or "including"; a semicolon cannot introduce a list.
qs.mk: [1|These islands were then the world's only source of two prized spices]⟨:⟩ [p:list|nutmeg and mace].

qs.passage: The ancient Romans built a road network that stretched for tens of thousands of kilometers. The most important roads were paved with stone and carefully engineered to last. A typical Roman road was built in several ______ a foundation of large stones, a middle layer of gravel or crushed rock, and a smooth surface of fitted paving stones. The roads were slightly curved so that rainwater would drain to the sides. Some of them, such as the Appian Way, are still in use today.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete clause introduces the list of layers.
qs.mk: [1|A typical Roman road was built in several layers]⟨:⟩ [p:list|a foundation of large stones, a middle layer of gravel or crushed rock, and a smooth surface of fitted paving stones].

qs.passage: Hearing begins when sound waves enter the ear canal and strike the eardrum. The human ear has three main ______ the outer ear, the middle ear, and the inner ear. The middle ear contains the three smallest bones in the body. The smallest of these, the stapes, is about the size of a grain of rice. In the inner ear, tiny hair cells convert vibrations into electrical signals that travel to the brain.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete clause introduces the list of three parts.
qs.mk: [1|The human ear has three main parts]⟨:⟩ [p:list|the outer ear, the middle ear, and the inner ear].

qs.passage: Qin Shi Huang became the first emperor of a unified China in 221 BCE. He standardized weights, measures, coins, and writing across his empire. He also ordered the construction of two enormous ______ an early version of the Great Wall and a vast tomb guarded by thousands of life-size clay soldiers. Farmers digging a well discovered the clay army in 1974. Archaeologists have uncovered only a small part of the tomb complex so far.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the two projects.
qs.mk: [1|He also ordered the construction of two enormous projects]⟨:⟩ [p:list|an early version of the Great Wall and a vast tomb guarded by thousands of life-size clay soldiers].

qs.passage: Ravens belong to the crow family, a group known for its intelligence. In laboratory studies, ravens have solved puzzles that challenge young children. They have also shown a skill once thought to be uniquely ______ for the future. In one experiment, ravens chose and saved a tool that they would need to open a box the next day. Researchers say that this ability likely evolved independently in birds and primates.
qs.exp: A colon after a complete clause introduces the specific skill. A semicolon needs a full clause after it.
qs.mk: [1|They have also shown a skill once thought to be uniquely human]⟨:⟩ [p:explanation|planning for the future].

qs.passage: Predicting volcanic eruptions can save thousands of lives. Before most eruptions, magma rises toward the surface and changes the volcano in measurable ways. Scientists therefore monitor active volcanoes for several warning ______ small earthquakes, swelling of the ground, and increased release of gases such as sulfur dioxide. In 1991, such signs allowed officials to evacuate tens of thousands of people before Mount Pinatubo erupted in the Philippines. Still, the exact timing of an eruption remains difficult to predict.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the list.
qs.mk: [1|Scientists therefore monitor active volcanoes for several warning signs]⟨:⟩ [p:list|small earthquakes, swelling of the ground, and increased release of gases such as sulfur dioxide].

qs.passage: Earth's atmosphere is a thin layer of gases held in place by gravity. It is made mostly of two ______ nitrogen, which makes up about 78 percent, and oxygen, which makes up about 21 percent. The remaining one percent includes argon, carbon dioxide, and water vapor. Although carbon dioxide is present only in small amounts, it plays an important role in trapping heat. Without the atmosphere, Earth's average temperature would be far below freezing.
qs.exp: Colon after a complete clause introduces the two gases. Never a colon right after a verb ("are") or "such as."
qs.mk: [1|It is made mostly of two gases]⟨:⟩ [p:list|nitrogen, which makes up about 78 percent, and oxygen, which makes up about 21 percent].

label: Colon traps (after verb / such as / including) ｜ 冒號陷阱

qs.passage: Mangrove forests grow along tropical coastlines where land meets the sea. Their tangled roots slow incoming waves and trap sediment. As a result, mangroves protect nearby communities ______ storm surges, erosion, and flooding. They also store large amounts of carbon in their waterlogged soils. Despite these benefits, many mangrove forests have been cleared for shrimp farms and coastal development.
qs.exp: No punctuation between a preposition ("from") and its object. A colon can only follow a complete independent clause.
qs.mk: {As a result}, [1:Subject + Verb|mangroves protect nearby communities from]⟨∅⟩[p:object of “from”|storm surges, erosion, and flooding].

qs.passage: A healthy honeybee hive contains three types of bees. The colony ______ a single queen, thousands of female worker bees, and a few hundred male drones. The queen lays up to 2,000 eggs a day during the summer. Workers gather food, build the comb, and defend the hive. Drones exist mainly to mate with queens from other colonies.
qs.exp: No colon (or any mark) between a verb and its object. A colon must follow a complete clause.
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|The colony includes]⟨∅⟩[p:object (list)|a single queen, thousands of female worker bees, and a few hundred male drones].

qs.passage: Before 1492, Europe, Asia, and Africa had no contact with the plants grown in the Americas. The exchange that followed Columbus's voyages transformed diets around the world. Many foods now considered staples elsewhere originated in the Americas, ______ potatoes, tomatoes, corn, and cacao. Italian cooking had no tomato sauce before the sixteenth century. Similarly, chili peppers did not reach India and Thailand until traders brought them from the Americas.
qs.exp: Never place a colon (or dash) right after "including." The list simply follows it.
qs.mk: [1|Many foods now considered staples elsewhere originated in the Americas]⟨,⟩ [p:example list|including potatoes, tomatoes, corn, and cacao].

qs.passage: The International Space Station orbits Earth about 16 times a day. The station has been continuously occupied since November 2000. Its crew members, who come from many countries, conduct experiments in ______ biology, physics, and medicine. Many experiments study how plants, animals, and people respond to long periods of weightlessness. The station is roughly the size of a football field, including its solar panels.
qs.exp: No colon after "such as"; a semicolon cannot introduce examples.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Its crew members]⟨,⟩ [d:nonessential|who come from many countries]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|conduct experiments in fields] ⟨∅⟩[p:examples|such as biology, physics, and medicine].

qs.passage: Mixing paints and mixing light produce very different results. When paints are combined, they absorb more light, so the mixture becomes darker. Light behaves in the opposite way. The three primary colors of light ______ red, green, and blue. When all three are combined in equal amounts, they produce white light, a principle used in television and computer screens.
qs.exp: No punctuation between a verb ("are") and what follows it.
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|The three primary colors of light are]⟨∅⟩[p:complement (list)|red, green, and blue].

qs.passage: The Arctic tundra is a treeless region where the ground beneath the surface stays frozen all year. Summers are short, and winters are long and dark. Despite these harsh conditions, the tundra supports many animals well adapted to the ______ caribou, arctic foxes, and snowy owls. Many birds migrate to the tundra each summer to nest. As the climate warms, shrubs are spreading northward into areas that were once open tundra.
qs.exp: No colon before or after "such as"; a comma introduces the examples.
qs.mk: [p|Despite these harsh conditions,] [1|the tundra supports many animals well adapted to the cold]⟨,⟩ [p:examples|such as caribou, arctic foxes, and snowy owls].

qs.passage: Caffeine is the most widely consumed stimulant in the world. It works by blocking a chemical in the brain called adenosine, which builds up during the day and makes people feel sleepy. Common sources of caffeine ______ coffee, tea, chocolate, and many soft drinks. The effects usually begin within about 15 to 45 minutes. Because caffeine can stay in the body for several hours, drinking it in the afternoon may interfere with sleep.
qs.exp: No punctuation between a verb ("include") and its objects.
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|Common sources of caffeine include]⟨∅⟩[p:object (list)|coffee, tea, chocolate, and many soft drinks].

label: Nonessential element: paired commas ｜ 非必要成分：成對逗號

qs.passage: Honeybee colonies make collective decisions in a surprisingly democratic way. When a colony needs a new home, a few hundred scout bees fly out to inspect possible sites. Each scout that finds a promising cavity returns and performs a waggle ______ which tells other bees the site's direction and distance. Over several days, more and more scouts join the dances for the best site. Once enough scouts gather at one location, the whole swarm takes off for its new home.
qs.exp: A nonessential "which" clause is set off with a comma. A semicolon or period would leave "which tells…" as a fragment; a colon cannot introduce a "which" clause.
qs.mk: [1|Each scout] [d|that finds a promising cavity] [1|returns and performs a waggle dance]⟨,⟩ [d:nonessential|which tells other bees the site's direction and distance].

qs.passage: Many people believe that reading on screens harms comprehension. A recent study of college students tested this belief directly. The ______ found that students who read printed texts remembered key details better than those who read the same texts on tablets. The difference was largest for long, complex passages. The researchers suggest that scrolling may make it harder for readers to build a mental map of a text.
qs.exp: "Though small" is a nonessential interrupter between subject and verb, so it needs a pair of commas. A semicolon would cut the subject off from its verb.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The study]⟨,⟩ [p:nonessential|though small]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|found] [d:noun clause|that students who read printed texts remembered key details better than those who read the same texts on tablets].

qs.passage: In the 1830s, the English mathematician Charles Babbage designed a machine called the Analytical Engine. The machine was never completed, but its design contained many features of modern computers. Ada Lovelace, the daughter of the poet Lord ______ wrote detailed notes explaining how the engine could work. Her notes included a step-by-step method for calculating a series of numbers called Bernoulli numbers. For this reason, she is often described as the first computer programmer.
qs.exp: The appositive "the daughter of the poet Lord Byron" opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Ada Lovelace]⟨,⟩ [p:nonessential appositive|the daughter of the poet Lord Byron]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|wrote detailed notes explaining how the engine could work].

qs.passage: For centuries, no one could read Egyptian hieroglyphs. The Rosetta Stone, a stone slab inscribed with the same decree in three ______ was discovered by French soldiers in Egypt in 1799. Two of the scripts were Egyptian, and the third was ancient Greek, which scholars could already read. By comparing the texts, the French scholar Jean-François Champollion deciphered the hieroglyphs in 1822. The stone is now displayed in the British Museum in London.
qs.exp: The appositive opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb "was discovered."
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The Rosetta Stone]⟨,⟩ [p:nonessential appositive|a stone slab inscribed with the same decree in three scripts]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|was discovered by French soldiers in Egypt in 1799].

qs.passage: Diamonds are made of carbon atoms arranged in a rigid crystal structure. Pure diamonds are colorless, but small amounts of other elements can tint them. The Hope Diamond, whose deep blue color comes from traces of the element ______ is one of the most famous gems in the world. It weighs about 45 carats. Since 1958, it has been displayed at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C.
qs.exp: The nonessential "whose" clause opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb "is."
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The Hope Diamond]⟨,⟩ [d:nonessential|whose deep blue color comes from traces of the element boron]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|is one of the most famous gems in the world].

qs.passage: Earth has just one natural satellite, the Moon. Several planets in our solar ______ including Jupiter and Saturn, have dozens of moons. Saturn has the most known moons of any planet. Many of these moons are only a few kilometers across. Mercury and Venus, by contrast, have no moons at all.
qs.exp: The nonessential phrase "including Jupiter and Saturn" closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma too.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Several planets in our solar system]⟨,⟩ [p:nonessential|including Jupiter and Saturn]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|have dozens of moons].

qs.passage: The Mariana Trench, the deepest known part of Earth's ______ lies in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Philippines. Its deepest point, called the Challenger Deep, is nearly 11,000 meters below the surface. If Mount Everest were placed there, its peak would still be about two kilometers underwater. Only a handful of people have ever visited the bottom. The first two, Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh, made the trip in 1960.
qs.exp: The appositive opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma (not a dash).
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The Mariana Trench]⟨,⟩ [p:nonessential appositive|the deepest known part of Earth's oceans]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|lies in the western Pacific Ocean, east of the Philippines].

qs.passage: Before the 1960s, scientists widely believed that only humans made and used tools. Jane Goodall, who began studying wild chimpanzees in Tanzania in ______ challenged that belief. She watched chimpanzees strip leaves from twigs and use them to fish termites out of their mounds. Her discovery forced scientists to rethink what made humans unique. Goodall's research continued for decades and transformed how people understand animal behavior.
qs.exp: The nonessential "who" clause opened with a comma, so it must close with a comma before the verb "challenged."
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Jane Goodall]⟨,⟩ [d:nonessential|who began studying wild chimpanzees in Tanzania in 1960]⟨,⟩ [1:Verb|challenged that belief].

label: Essential element: no commas ｜ 必要成分：不加逗號

qs.passage: The discovery of DNA's double-helix structure in 1953 is usually credited to James Watson and Francis Crick. Their work, however, relied heavily on data gathered by other scientists. In 1952, British chemist ______ produced an X-ray image of DNA known as Photo 51. Watson saw the image without her knowledge, and it helped him confirm the molecule's helical shape. Franklin died in 1958, four years before Watson, Crick, and Maurice Wilkins received the Nobel Prize.
qs.exp: Title + name ("British chemist Rosalind Franklin") with no "the" is essential, so no commas. A comma before the verb "produced" separates subject and verb.
qs.mk: [p|In 1952,] [1:Subject|British chemist Rosalind Franklin]⟨∅⟩[1:Verb|produced an X-ray image of DNA known as Photo 51].

qs.passage: Rachel Carson is best known for Silent Spring, her 1962 book about the dangers of pesticides. That book helped launch the modern environmental movement. However, the ______ made Carson famous was an earlier work about the ocean. The Sea Around Us, published in 1951, spent more than 80 weeks on the New York Times bestseller list. Its success allowed Carson to leave her government job and write full-time.
qs.exp: A "that" clause is essential and never takes commas. A comma before the verb "made" would also separate subject and verb.
qs.mk: {However}, [1:Subject|the book]⟨∅⟩[d:essential clause|that first made Carson famous]⟨∅⟩[1:Verb|was an earlier work about the ocean].

qs.passage: In the summer of 1816, a group of writers gathered at a villa near Lake Geneva in Switzerland. Stormy weather kept them indoors, so they challenged one another to write ghost stories. Mary Shelley, then just 18 years old, began a story that would become one of the most famous novels ever written. The novel ______ is often considered the first work of science fiction. It tells the story of a scientist who creates life and then abandons his creation.
qs.exp: The title identifies which novel (essential), so no commas. A single comma would also split subject and verb.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The novel Frankenstein]⟨∅⟩[1:Verb|is often considered the first work of science fiction].

qs.passage: In 1903, Wilbur and Orville Wright made the first controlled, powered airplane flight near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. That first flight lasted only 12 seconds and covered about 120 feet. The brothers' success depended less on engine power than on control. Their system of wing warping—twisting the wingtips to roll the aircraft into a ______ allowed the pilot to keep the plane balanced. Later aircraft replaced wing warping with hinged panels called ailerons, but the principle remained the same.
qs.exp: The interruption opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash. Mixing a dash with a comma (or using nothing) breaks the pair.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Their system of wing warping]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|twisting the wingtips to roll the aircraft into a turn]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|allowed the pilot to keep the plane balanced].

qs.passage: In 2019, astronomers released the first image of a black hole. The picture shows a glowing ring of hot gas surrounding a dark center. Producing it was an enormous technical challenge. The project linked eight radio observatories—located on four different ______ that together functioned as a single telescope the size of Earth. The black hole, which sits at the center of the galaxy M87, is about 55 million light-years away.
qs.exp: The interrupting phrase opened with a dash, so it must close with a dash.
qs.mk: [1|The project linked eight radio observatories]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|located on four different continents]⟨—⟩[d|that together functioned as a single telescope the size of Earth].

qs.passage: Mount Everest grows a little taller each year. The Indian tectonic plate continues to push northward into the Eurasian plate, lifting the Himalayas upward. The rate of growth—about four millimeters per ______ is tiny compared with the mountain's total height. Everest's official height of 8,849 meters was announced jointly by China and Nepal in 2020. Earthquakes and erosion can also slightly change the mountain's height over time.
qs.exp: Opening dash → closing dash.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The rate of growth]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|about four millimeters per year]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|is tiny compared with the mountain's total height].

qs.passage: A total solar eclipse occurs when the moon passes directly between Earth and the sun. For a few minutes, the sky darkens and the sun's glowing outer atmosphere, the corona, becomes visible. Total solar eclipses—though visible somewhere on Earth about every 18 ______ occur at any single location only about once every 375 years on average. As a result, many people travel great distances to see one. In April 2024, millions of people gathered along a narrow path from Mexico to Canada to watch the event.
qs.exp: Opening dash → closing dash. (Note "though visible…" inside is a reduced conjunction clause.)
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Total solar eclipses]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|though visible somewhere on Earth about every 18 months]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|occur at any single location only about once every 375 years on average].

qs.passage: The bristlecone pines of California's White Mountains are among the oldest living things on Earth. One tree—nicknamed Methuselah by the researchers who studied ______ is estimated to be more than 4,800 years old. The trees grow extremely slowly in the cold, dry mountain air. Their dense wood resists insects, fungi, and decay. To protect Methuselah from vandals, the Forest Service keeps its exact location secret.
qs.exp: Opening dash → closing dash.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|One tree]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|nicknamed Methuselah by the researchers who studied it]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|is estimated to be more than 4,800 years old].

qs.passage: The kiwi—a flightless bird found only in New ______ lays one of the largest eggs relative to body size of any bird. A female kiwi's egg can weigh about a fifth of her body weight. Carrying it is a huge burden, and in the final days before laying, the female has little room left to eat. Kiwis are also unusual in having nostrils at the tip of their long bills. They use their keen sense of smell to find worms and insects in the soil at night.
qs.exp: Opening dash → closing dash.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The kiwi]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|a flightless bird found only in New Zealand]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|lays one of the largest eggs relative to body size of any bird].

qs.passage: Tardigrades—microscopic animals often called water ______ can survive conditions that would kill almost any other creature. When their environment dries out, they curl up and enter a state in which their metabolism nearly stops. In this state, they can withstand extreme cold and heat for short periods. In 2007, tardigrades survived ten days exposed to outer space. When water returns, they can revive and resume normal life.
qs.exp: Opening dash → closing dash.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Tardigrades]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|microscopic animals often called water bears]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|can survive conditions that would kill almost any other creature].

qs.passage: Glass frogs—so called because the skin on their bellies is ______ live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Through this see-through skin, an observer can watch the frog's heart beating. While sleeping, the frogs can hide most of their red blood cells in their livers, making their bodies even more transparent. This trick helps them avoid predators during the day. Scientists hope that studying it could lead to new treatments for blood clots.
qs.exp: Opening dash → closing dash.
qs.mk: [1:Subject|Glass frogs]⟨—⟩[p:nonessential|so called because the skin on their bellies is transparent]⟨—⟩[1:Verb|live in the rainforests of Central and South America].

qs.passage: Ancient Roman concrete has survived for two thousand years in harbors and monuments. Modern concrete, by contrast, can crack within decades. Scientists studying Roman structures have identified one likely reason for the ______ lumps of lime that can react with water to seal cracks as they form. This self-healing ability may help explain why Roman harbor walls are still standing. Engineers are now testing whether similar ingredients could make modern concrete more durable.
qs.exp: A single dash after a complete clause can introduce an explanation (like a colon). A semicolon or period would leave "small lumps…" as a fragment (no verb).
qs.mk: [1|Scientists studying Roman structures have identified one likely reason for the difference]⟨—⟩[p:explanation|small lumps of lime] [d|that can react with water to seal cracks as they form].

qs.passage: The axolotl is a salamander native to the lakes around Mexico City. Unlike most salamanders, it keeps its feathery gills and lives in water its entire life. The axolotl also has an extraordinary ______ can regrow lost limbs, parts of its heart, and even portions of its brain. Scientists study the animal in hopes of learning how to improve healing in humans. In the wild, however, axolotls are critically endangered because of pollution and urban growth.
qs.exp: A single dash after a complete clause can introduce an explanation. A comma = comma splice; nothing = run-on.
qs.mk: [1|The axolotl also has an extraordinary ability]⟨—⟩[2|it can regrow lost limbs, parts of its heart, and even portions of its brain].

qs.passage: Coast redwoods grow only in a narrow strip along the Pacific coast of California and southern Oregon. They thrive in the region's frequent summer fog, which provides moisture. The tallest known living tree is one of these redwoods in ______ giant named Hyperion that stands about 116 meters tall. Its exact location is kept secret to protect it from damage. Officials have even banned visitors from the area after hikers trampled the surrounding soil.
qs.exp: A dash can introduce a phrase that renames/explains. A semicolon or period would leave "a giant named Hyperion…" as a fragment (no main verb).
qs.mk: [1|The tallest known living tree is one of these redwoods in California]⟨—⟩[p:explanation|a giant named Hyperion] [d|that stands about 116 meters tall].

qs.passage: During the colonial era, European powers established huge plantations in tropical regions. Workers on these plantations, many of them enslaved or forced laborers, grew crops for export to Europe. Sugar, cotton, rubber, and ______ crops shaped the economies of entire regions for centuries. In many former colonies, the effects can still be seen in patterns of land ownership. Some countries still depend heavily on exporting a single crop.
qs.exp: A dash can separate an introductory list from the clause that sums it up ("these crops"). A comma creates a confusing run-on structure.
qs.mk: [p:list (summed up by “these”)|Sugar, cotton, rubber, and coffee]⟨—⟩[1|these crops shaped the economies of entire regions for centuries].

label: No punctuation between subject–verb / verb–object / prep–object ｜ 禁止加標點的位置

qs.passage: Tomatoes originated in western South America and were brought to Europe in the 1500s. Italians and Spaniards soon began cooking with them. In parts of northern Europe, however, the plant was grown mainly as a decoration. The belief that tomatoes might be ______ was common there for many years, partly because the plant belongs to the same family as deadly nightshade. By the 1800s, tomatoes had become a popular ingredient across the continent.
qs.exp: The whole phrase "The belief that tomatoes might be poisonous" is the subject; no punctuation can separate a subject from its verb ("was").
qs.mk: [1:Subject|The belief that tomatoes might be poisonous]⟨∅⟩[1:Verb|was common there for many years]⟨,⟩ [p|partly] «because»[d|the plant belongs to the same family as deadly nightshade].

qs.passage: Learning to play a musical instrument requires coordinating the eyes, ears, and hands. Researchers have found ______ children who take music lessons often show improvements in memory and attention. It is not yet clear whether music itself causes these benefits. Children who take lessons may differ in other ways, such as family income or parental involvement. Long-term studies that randomly assign children to music lessons may help answer the question.
qs.exp: No punctuation between a verb ("found") and its object clause ("that…").
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|Researchers have found]⟨∅⟩[d:noun clause (object)|that children who take music lessons often show improvements in memory and attention].

qs.passage: Sunlight contains all the colors of the rainbow. As it passes through the atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules. The reason the sky looks blue is ______ these molecules scatter short blue wavelengths of light much more than longer red ones. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more of the atmosphere before reaching our eyes. By then, much of the blue light has been scattered away, leaving the sky orange and red.
qs.exp: No punctuation between "is" and its complement clause "that…". A colon needs a complete clause before it.
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|The reason the sky looks blue is]⟨∅⟩[d:noun clause (complement)|that these molecules scatter short blue wavelengths of light much more than longer red ones].

qs.passage: Dinosaurs dominated life on land for more than 150 million years. For a long time, they were imagined as slow, cold-blooded creatures similar to modern lizards. Scientists are still debating ______ dinosaurs were warm-blooded like birds or cold-blooded like reptiles. Evidence from bone growth rings suggests that many dinosaurs grew quickly, a trait associated with warm-bloodedness. Some researchers now argue that dinosaurs fell somewhere between the two categories.
qs.exp: No punctuation between the verb "debating" and its object clause "whether…".
qs.mk: [1:Subject + Verb|Scientists are still debating]⟨∅⟩[d:noun clause (object)|whether dinosaurs were warm-blooded like birds or cold-blooded like reptiles].

qs.passage: The giant anteater of Central and South America has no teeth. Instead, it uses a sticky tongue up to 60 centimeters long to collect insects. Its diet consists almost entirely ______ ants and termites. An anteater can eat about 30,000 insects in a single day. To avoid destroying its food supply, it feeds at each nest for only a minute or so before moving on.
qs.exp: No punctuation between a preposition ("of") and its object.
qs.mk: [1|Its diet consists almost entirely of]⟨∅⟩[p:object of “of”|ants and termites].
